title: Record, rough-cut and design YouTube videos with agents
summary: A creator open-sourced the system they use for YouTube: a teleprompter, agents that transcribe takes and propose a cut, and animated graphics, with human review of every cut.
agent_role: Agents transcribe takes, sync camera and audio, propose a candidate cut, flag possible errors, and help plan and build graphics. The human reviews and approves the cut and finishes in a normal video editor.
what_they_did: Sirio Berati shared his YouTube workflow. You read a script on a teleprompter that records your takes. An agent transcribes them, lines up camera and audio, and suggests a cut. You review it in an editing app. Then you design animated graphics from the final transcript and hand files to Resolve or Premiere.
worth_knowing: The author warns it is not a one-click editor. Speech recognition can spell a fumbled word correctly, and silence does not prove a word ended, so cuts need human review.
prompt: Help me edit my YouTube video from raw takes. Here is my script [script file] and my recordings folder [folder path]. Transcribe every take, mark flubbed lines, and pick the best take for each part of the script. Write a proposed cut list with start and end times as a file, and list any spots where you are unsure. Don't overwrite my original files. Then, from the approved transcript, draft a short brief for on-screen graphics for each section. Wait for my review before exporting anything.

curation.rationale: A real agent-assisted video editing workflow with code, but the README mostly describes parts and gives no concrete reported result from using it.
